description: The ledger text contract (contract/README.md, rules.json LEDGER_TEXT). For each byte fixture in this folder: how many lines it has, which are blank, which are unreadable and why, how the readable rows group (key: the usable request id, or "line <n>" for a row without one; lines in file order, groups in first appearance order), and each readable row's cap_charge as a known amount (null when it is not one). imd-flop/test/ledger-text.test.ts and viewer/test_ledger_text.py read every fixture and check these same expectations.

empty.jsonl.note: an empty file has no lines

no-final-newline.jsonl.note: a last line with no \n is still a line

torn-last-line.jsonl.note: a torn last line (a writer that died mid line) is unreadable under its own number

cr-joined.jsonl.note: finding 6: lines end at \n only, so two rows joined by a bare \r are one line, and it is not valid JSON

cr-between-tokens.jsonl.note: finding 6b: a \r between tokens is JSON whitespace; the damaged line after it is line 2

crlf.jsonl.note: a \r before the \n is JSON whitespace: both rows read

unit-separators.jsonl.note: finding 6c: \x1c to \x1f are not in the blank set, so a line of one of them is unreadable

nel.jsonl.note: U+0085 (C2 85) is not in the blank set; a bare 0x85 byte decodes to U+FFFD, not blank either

blank-set.jsonl.note: every character of the blank set makes a blank line; blank lines are numbered

bom.jsonl.note: a BOM before a row: JSON.parse does not skip it, so line 1 is unreadable

invalid-utf8-in-string.jsonl.note: finding 8: an invalid byte inside a string becomes U+FFFD; the row reads and counts

invalid-utf8-between-tokens.jsonl.note: an invalid byte between tokens becomes U+FFFD, which is not JSON: that line only is unreadable

json-constants.jsonl.note: item 7 of pass 3: NaN, Infinity and -Infinity are not JSON

numbers-as-doubles.jsonl.note: a number is a double: a 4300 digit integer and 1e400 are Infinity, 2^53 + 1 is 2^53; none of those is a known amount. 2^53 - 1 is read exactly, and it is not a known amount either: it is above AMOUNT_MAX, 1e9 FLOP (swarm audit 33f3b9f, finding 5; it was a known amount when AMOUNT_MAX was 2^53 - 1)

booleans.jsonl.note: a boolean is never a number: false is not 0

not-objects.jsonl.note: valid JSON that is not an object is unreadable as not a JSON object

control-char-in-string.jsonl.note: a raw control character inside a string is not JSON

escapes.jsonl.note: escaped lone surrogates, U+2028 and NUL are valid JSON strings

request-id-groups.jsonl.note: rows group by a usable request id

request-id-unusable.jsonl.note: finding 7: a request id that is not REQUEST_ID (a space, null, empty, 129 characters, a number) groups nothing: each line is its own group

duplicate-keys.jsonl.note: a duplicate key: the last one wins in both parts

torn-line-then-row.jsonl.note: the writer rule: a row appended after a torn last line starts on a fresh line, so the torn line stays unreadable under its own number and the new row is whole

depth-32.jsonl.note: the nesting limit (swarm audit 33f3b9f, finding 8): a row nested 32 levels deep, the row object included, is at the limit and is a row

depth-33.jsonl.note: 33 levels is over the limit: unreadable, nested too deep. Line 2 is not valid JSON either, and it is still nested too deep: depth is counted on the text before parsing

depth-10000.jsonl.note: 10000 levels: nested too deep in both parts. JSON.parse reads it and Python's json raises RecursionError, so without the limit the two parts read it differently

depth-brackets-in-strings.jsonl.note: brackets inside a string do not count, an escaped quote does not end the string, and an escaped backslash before the closing quote does not escape it: depth 3

lone-surrogate.jsonl.note: a lone surrogate escape, as an older version's cut could leave one (review of the audit 33f3b9f fixes, defect 11): JSON.parse reads it, and the viewer reads it too and shows U+FFFD in its place, so its page still builds

depth-siblings.jsonl.note: forty sibling arrays and two sibling objects at the same level: each ] and } closes its level, so the depth stays 3 and the line is a row

depth-unbalanced-closers.jsonl.note: closers before any opener count too: depth goes to -4, then 33 openers reach 29, under the limit, so these lines are not valid JSON rather than nested too deep. The count is never floored at 0
